statement: A weighted graph is a graph whose vertices or edges have been assigned weights, where a weight is a numerical value assigned as a label to a vertex or edge of the graph.

properties.property: A vertex-weighted graph has weights on its vertices and an edge-weighted graph has weights on its edges.
properties.why: Distinguishes whether weights are assigned to vertices or edges of the graph

properties.property: The weight of a subgraph is the sum of the weights of the vertices or edges within that subgraph.
properties.why: Defines how the weight of a subgraph is aggregated from its elements

properties.property: A weight is a numerical value assigned as a label to a vertex or edge of a graph.
properties.why: Specifies that the assigned label must be numerical

properties.property: An unweighted graph is a graph whose vertices and edges have not been assigned weights, representing the opposite of a weighted graph.
properties.why: Contrasts weighted graphs with graphs lacking weight assignments

assumptions.assumption: Weights assigned to vertices or edges are numerical values.
assumptions.breaks_when: Labels assigned to vertices or edges are non-numerical or omitted.

assumptions.assumption: The underlying structure is a graph consisting of vertices connected in pairs by edges.
assumptions.breaks_when: The structure is not a graph.

failure_modes.signature: Neither vertices nor edges have assigned weights
failure_modes.cause: No weights have been assigned to any vertex or edge of the graph.

failure_modes.signature: Inability to compute the weight of a subgraph as a sum
failure_modes.cause: Vertices or edges within the subgraph lack assigned numerical weights.

instantiation.why_here: In agrios_ws, smacplannerhybrid relies on a weighted graph to model the robot's state-space for path planning. The component's planning algorithm requires this representation so that edge weights encode traversal distances and motion penalties to search for a minimal-cost trajectory.

concrete.in_your_project: The search space graph traversed by the smacplannerhybrid planning algorithm
The set of discrete search states representing robot poses considered by the planner
The set of valid motion primitives or transitions connecting reachable poses, weighted by traversal cost
